notes:
Summary: Calypso is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency, high-throughput conversational workflows used by trader support tools. Primary ask: firm latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) across streaming and non-streaming modes plus an agreed measurement methodology they can share with compliance. They want reserved GPU planning guidance for predictable throughput and hard SLA terms for p99 under load.

Context / initial ask:
- Use cases: (1) operator chat (real-time Q&A) with token streaming to UI, (2) nightly reranking jobs for instrument lists, (3) embeddings for similarity search.
- Traffic shape: spikey batch loads at market open + steady conversational RPS during trading hours. Expected 1k concurrent chat sessions peak, ~250k embed ops/day.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-to-high; will commit to 12-month reserved capacity if SLO and measurement align.

Latency SLO discussion notes (from 2026-02-04 call):
- Calypso SRE requested explicit definitions: p50/p95/p99 must be measured both client-side (end-to-end) and server-side (post-proxy). They emphasized discrepancies between browser perceived latency (WS framing, first-chunk) and server token gen timing.
- Proposed target (starting point): non-streaming generation: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms for typical short prompts (<=128 tokens). Streaming: first-chunk (TTFC) p95 <= 150ms, subsequent-chunk p95 <= 60ms for 64-token chunks.
- Calypso wants metrics separated by model variant (base vs quantized), route (dedicated pool vs fallback hosted), and region.
- Agreed measurement dimensions: percentile, sample size, measurement window, and whether cold KV-cache included.

Measurement alignment / methodology we proposed:
- Two parallel measurement streams:
  - Synthetic load harness (server-side): controlled load generator in their VPC hitting dedicated endpoints via configured routing. Measures server-side receive-to-last-token-generated (server processing time) and per-token delta for streaming.
  - Client-side E2E telemetry: browser/agent-level timing (WS open -> first-byte -> last-byte), includes network, TLS, and client serialization.
- Reconciliation step: correlate APM traces (span id mapping) so a single request id maps client and server metrics; compute delta for network/proxy overhead.
- Instrumentation requirements: request-id propagation header, sample rate 100% for p99 debug window (48-hour trial), and aggregated histograms (HDR or HdrHistogram output) exported to their metrics backend.
- Measurement rules: exclude synthetic maintenance windows, mark cold-starts (server warm-up < 2 min) and treat as separate bucket, cache-hit vs cache-miss labelled.

POC / Dedicated sizing notes:
- For their conversational workload (1k concurrent), approximate reserved capacity recommended: 8 x high-memory A100-class GPUs (or equivalent A10g * 12) with autoscaling buffer + burst pool. Rationale: sustained per-GPU throughput for 4k tokens/sec aggregate with KV cache and batching.
- Suggested config: 2 dedicated pools: latency-first (pinned models, smaller batch targets, aggressive pre-warming) and throughput-first (larger batch sizes for reranking and embedding pipelines).
- Fallback policy: route to hosted compatible quantized variant with circuit-breaker; Calypso asked for SLA credit trigger if fallback used >1% of requests over 24h.

SLA negotiation points (Calypso priorities):
- Hard p99 targets with measurement method spelled out (who measures, how, exclusion windows).
- Credits for sustained misses: sliding window approach (24h), threshold-based (p99 miss > 0.5% of requests triggers 5% credit, >2% triggers 15%).
- Uptime: 99.95% for dedicated pool.
- Data residency and audit logs: retention 1 year for request traces; KMS usage for keys.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-01-15: initial intro call (AE Dana + SE Harpreet) – high level requirements captured.
- 2026-01-22: security questionnaire sent (Calypso infosec).
- 2026-02-04: latency SLO deep dive + CTO on call (notes above). Fireflies id ff_2026-02-04_6721.
- 2026-02-18: Redwood sent draft dedicated proposal + sizing spreadsheet (/drive/pricing/decks/calypso-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf).
- 2026-02-26: Calypso returned procurement constraints (Q2 budget) + asked for 48-hour staged p99 trial on staging dedicated pool. Jira INF-2319 opened for trial orchestration.

Open risks / blockers:
- Procurement needs Q2 budget sign-off (may push to May).
- SOC2 evidence: calypso wants end-to-end proof of request-level audit logs and KMS integration before exec sign-off.
- Network egress: legal needs written VPC peering egress policy.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood to deliver SLO measurement playbook (detailed doc) and instrumentation checklist by 2026-03-12.
- Schedule a 90-minute latency workshop with SREs (deep dive on tracing, HdrHistogram exports, and token-chunking for streaming) – target slot week of 2026-03-22.
- Run 48-hour p99/p95 staging run with synthetic harness (SE Harpreet to coordinate). Capture both client E2E and server-side histograms; Redwood to provide Grafana dashboard template.
- Legal to propose SLA credit language matching Calypso threshold asks (AE Dana to loop legal).

Notes / snippets from CTO: "We need deterministic inference economics — if you promise p99 you must show measurement we can trust (not just server timers). Also, streaming behavior drives UX more than raw p50; first-chunk perception is critical."

Sales notes (short):
- High probability if staging run meets p99 in two week window and security answers provided.
- Upsell: 12-month reserved + Optimize add-on for batching/cache tuning.
